sections.heading: Texas fault and comparative negligence
paragraphs: Texas follows modified comparative negligence with a 51% bar. If you are more than 50% at fault, you may recover nothing. Insurers in Rio Grande Valley routinely argue shared fault to reduce payouts—your documentation from day one shapes that fight.

Police reports, witness statements, traffic citations, and scene photos help establish who failed to yield, follow speed limits, or maintain a safe distance. Never admit fault at the scene; describe facts calmly to officers.
list: Request the responding officer's name and report number
Note weather, lighting, and road conditions
Identify surveillance cameras at nearby businesses
Save dashcam or phone video immediately

sections.heading: Rio Grande Valley insurance minimums and coverage gaps
paragraphs: Texas requires minimum liability limits of 30/60/25 ($30,000 per person bodily injury, $60,000 per accident, $25,000 property damage). Many at-fault drivers carry only minimums—often insufficient for hospital bills after a serious Rio Grande Valley collision.

Review your declarations page for uninsured/underinsured motorist (UM/UIM), personal injury protection (PIP), and MedPay. These coverages can matter when the other driver has inadequate limits or flees the scene.

sections.heading: Medical treatment and documentation
paragraphs: Insurers scrutinize gaps in treatment. After a Rio Grande Valley crash, seek care within 24 hours even if pain feels minor—whiplash, concussion, and internal bleeding may appear later. ER records, urgent care notes, and follow-up visits create a timeline insurers cannot easily dismiss.

Keep itemized bills, imaging orders (X-ray, MRI, CT), prescriptions, physical therapy schedules, and mileage to appointments. Bobby Garcia Law's medical specialists help clients organize treatment records for maximum clarity.
list: Photograph visible injuries on day one
Do not sign blanket medical authorizations for adjusters
Track lost wages with employer documentation

sections.heading: Dealing with claims adjusters
paragraphs: Adjusters represent the insurance company's financial interests—not yours. They may request recorded statements, broad medical releases, or quick settlements before you understand injury severity. In Rio Grande Valley and across Texas, early statements can lock in descriptions that reduce fault on the other driver.

Provide basic facts—date, time, location, vehicles involved. Decline recorded interviews until you understand coverage and injuries. Request denials, reservation-of-rights letters, and settlement offers in writing.

sections.heading: Evidence preservation in the first 30 days
paragraphs: Skid marks fade, witnesses forget details, and business surveillance video is often deleted within 7–30 days. After a crash on Rio Grande Valley highways or surface streets, send preservation letters to businesses, municipalities, and trucking companies when commercial vehicles are involved.

Preserve repair estimates, rental receipts, tow bills, and cell-phone metadata. Social media posts about the crash or your activities can be used against you—avoid discussing fault or activities online.

sections.heading: Commercial trucks and 18-wheelers
paragraphs: Rio Grande Valley corridors see heavy commercial traffic. Trucking cases involve federal motor carrier rules, electronic logging devices, black-box data, and multiple defendants (driver, carrier, broker, shipper). Evidence spoils quickly—qualified counsel helps preserve downloads and driver qualification files.

sections.heading: Statute of limitations and notice deadlines
paragraphs: Most Texas personal injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury date. Government-entity cases (city buses, state vehicles) may require earlier notice—sometimes within months. Missing a deadline can permanently bar recovery regardless of merit.
Calendar your dates immediately after a Rio Grande Valley crash. Bobby Garcia Law offers free consultations 24/7 at (956) 668-7400 to help you understand timelines—Justice Made Simple.

sections.heading: Property damage and total-loss disputes
paragraphs: Insurers may undervalue repairs or declare a total loss based on comparables that favor the carrier. Obtain independent estimates from reputable body shops in Rio Grande Valley. Review valuation reports for missing equipment, recent maintenance, and regional price adjustments.

sections.heading: Lost wages and economic damages
paragraphs: Document every missed shift, PTO day, and reduced earning capacity. Employers in Rio Grande Valley can provide verification letters; self-employed victims should gather tax returns, contracts, and invoices showing lost opportunities. Vocational experts may be needed for long-term disability.

sections.heading: Pain, suffering, and non-economic damages
paragraphs: Texas allows recovery for physical pain, mental anguish, disfigurement, and loss of enjoyment of life when liability and causation are established. Journals documenting sleep loss, anxiety, and daily limitations can support these elements—start early after your Rio Grande Valley collision.

sections.heading: Settlement vs. litigation timeline
paragraphs: Minor property claims may resolve in weeks; injury claims with treatment, disputed fault, or commercial defendants often take months or years. Mediation, discovery, and expert depositions extend timelines but may increase recovery. Never sign a general release while treatment is ongoing.

faq.question: Should I give a recorded statement to insurance after a Rio Grande Valley crash?
faq.answer: Generally, provide basic facts only until you understand injuries and coverage. Recorded statements can be used against you—consult counsel before agreeing.

faq.question: What does no win, no fee mean?
faq.answer: On qualifying personal injury cases, Bobby Garcia Law typically works on contingency—you owe no attorney fee unless we recover compensation. Confirm terms in your fee agreement.

faq.question: How long do I have to file in Texas after a Rio Grande Valley accident?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a two-year statute of limitations, but exceptions apply for minors, government entities, and wrongful death. Verify your dates immediately.

faq.question: Does Bobby Garcia Law handle Spanish-speaking clients?
faq.answer: Yes. Our team is fully bilingual—English and Español—24 hours a day, seven days a week.
